Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Acute upper respiratory symptoms for ~5 days: dry, hacking cough; runny nose; myalgias; intermittent headache; chills. No hemoptysis, dyspnea, or wheeze. Telemedicine oropharynx with mild erythema, no tonsillar enlargement; no neck lymphadenopathy reported. Background T2DM and hypertension on metformin and lisinopril; home blood sugars stable; patient-reported BP normal today.
- Most consistent with viral upper respiratory infection. DDx supports consideration of influenza and COVID-19 given systemic symptoms; ACE inhibitor–related cough less likely due to abrupt onset with coryzal features.
- No red flags requiring urgent in-person assessment identified in transcript.

Management Plan
- Supportive care advised: over-the-counter “Day Nurse/Night Nurse” permitted with current meds per clinician.  
- Safety-net: seek care if shortness of breath, wheeze, worsening systemic symptoms, or if symptoms persist >3 weeks; consider in-person exam if symptoms change or worsen.  
- No prescriptions issued. No tests ordered. Continue home monitoring of blood glucose and blood pressure as usual.
